meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: private law in Quebec governed by the Civil Code of Quebec; federal and public law governed by common law

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons, CQLR c. P-45; Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1 (Quebec); FINTRAC reporting and beneficial ownership guidance; Quebec ultimate beneficiary register requirements under P-45 and its regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of each ultimate beneficial owner's passport and current proof of address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or authorized Commissioner for Oaths in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the designated Competent Authority of the UBO's home jurisdiction; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Canadian Embassy or High Commission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the corporate UBO's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization via the local competent authority and Canadian diplomatic post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing a Quebec-based incorporator or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if executed outside Canada; if executed in Canada, domestic notarization or commissioner of oaths is sufficient

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration of registration containing director appointments and UBO schedule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder or director before a Quebec notary or authorized commissioner of oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization only; no apostille required for filing within Quebec with the Registraire d'entreprises

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified UBOs, directors, and senior officers against (i) Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian autonomous sanctions lists and Special Economic Measures Act regulations; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated list; (iii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists where any U.S. nexus exists; (iv) domestic PEP databases and federal and provincial conflict-of-interest registers. Enhanced due diligence applies if an UBO is a PEP, is resident in a FATF-monitored jurisdiction, or holds an interest through a trust, nominee, or bearer-share arrangement. For this low-risk micro-SaaS with subscription card payments via Paddle and Lemon Squeezy, simplified CDD is permitted when no sanctions/PEP alerts arise and the source of funds is demonstrably low-risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire d'entreprises du Québec – Répertoire des entreprises and online name reservation service (www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every corporate name must have a French-language form. A non-French version may be registered only if a French version is also registered and is used at least as prominently in Quebec. Names must be formed using Latin characters and must respect the linguistic standards of the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11. Foreign names must be transliterated or translated for the legal designation (dénomination sociale); English generic words are scrutinized unless part of a registered trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 90 days and may be renewed only by filing a new reservation application before expiry; there is no formal statutory extension mechanism. If the name reservation is refused, the applicant must file a written application for administrative review (demande d'examen de décision) with the Registraire d'entreprises within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching a fresh Quebec name-search report and evidence of distinctiveness. A further refusal may be appealed to the Court of Québec (Civil Division) by way of judicial review within 30 days of the administrative decision. Where the refusal is grounded in non-conformity with the Charter of the French Language, an application for derogation or approval must be submitted to the Office québécois de la langue française before re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for a low-risk micro-SaaS business, provided the virtual office includes a physical street address in Quebec at which legal process and corporate documents may be personally served during regular business hours. P.O. boxes and bare mail-drop addresses are insufficient. Co-working spaces and registered-agent office addresses are commonly accepted; however, the Registraire d'entreprises and tax authorities retain discretion to require proof of a genuine connection, such as a lease, local staff presence, or corporate records maintained at the address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated 5% annual probability of an unannounced compliance inspection for an online-only micro-SaaS with no inventory and no physical plant. The probability increases to approximately 15–20% if the registered office is a shared virtual-office address or a high-volume mail-forwarding facility.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 25 (incorporation), 28 (articles), 46 (registered office), 48 (first directors), 59 (share register) and 60 (minute books).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution (Articles of Incorporation) filed through the REQ Online Incorporation Service
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital under the Quebec Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued for future services and paid in later; no escrow account is required for ordinary share subscriptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that: (1) the registered office of the Corporation shall be situated at the address stated in the articles of incorporation in the Province of Quebec; (2) the by-laws presented to this meeting are adopted as By-Law No. 1; (3) the directors are authorized to accept share subscriptions and to issue founder common shares to the initial subscribers; (4) the directors named in the articles are confirmed as the first directors; (5) [Name] is appointed President and [Name] is appointed Secretary; and (6) the directors and officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute all filings, and pay registration fees with Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name validation and optional name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a legal name check against the REQ corporate database and, if protection is desired, file a name reservation request through the REQ online portal. The proposed name must not be misleading, prohibited, or contrary to public order; a distinctive English, French, or bilingual name with a Quebec legal element such as Inc. or Corp. is acceptable for a micro-SaaS business.
required_dossiers: Completed online name reservation form
Contact and mailing address in Quebec
Proof of authority for the representative, if filed by a mandatary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on distinctiveness or linguistic grounds, file a revised name request or obtain a written consent from the holder of an existing prior name; REQ will process a fresh reservation without penalization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of articles of incorporation and initial director declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — secure online incorporation module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online questionnaire for incorporations, setting out the authorized capital (e.g. unlimited common shares without par value), initial registered office in Quebec, and the first directors. Electronic signatures of the incorporators are accepted; notarization is not required for standard articles of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Statutory articles of incorporation (statuts de constitution) generated online
Identity details of founders and first directors
Authorization resolution if an incorporator is a corporation
Statistical activity code 6201 / NAICS 511210 for the principal business
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query for missing or inconsistent information, correct the flagged fields in the online application and resubmit. No additional fee is payable if the rejected filing did not reach issuance stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of certificate of incorporation and federal/provincial tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Canada Revenue Agency / Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate of incorporation is issued, obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), then register through CRA and Revenu Québec for the federal Business Number, GST/HST, QST, corporate income tax, and any payroll deductions. The registrations are mandatory for a micro-SaaS operating in Quebec and can be coordinated online through the tax portals.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (certificat de constitution)
NEQ number assigned by REQ
Directors and officers identification
Federal GST/HST and Quebec QST registration request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration portal cannot verify the NEQ due to a data transfer delay, wait 24 hours and reattempt, or contact Revenu Québec's business counter to synchronize the REQ-CRA records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational formalities, by-laws, and statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation and corporate secretary / legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting or use written unanimous resolutions to adopt By-Law No. 1, approve the share subscription agreement, issue founder common shares, appoint officers, approve banking signatories, and ratify the registered office address. The statutory registers, including the share register and directors register, must be maintained at the corporation's records office in Quebec.
required_dossiers: Minutes or unanimous resolution of the first board meeting
By-Law No. 1 establishing governance rules
Share subscription statements and share certificates
Registered office consent form from the building owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer appointment or by-law adoption is formally defective, the board may ratify the action by way of a subsequent board resolution; any director consent defect is cured by obtaining written unanimous consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal occupancy and commercial premises compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality — permits and inspections division for the chosen Quebec city
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a physical office, verify that the leased premises are zoned for office use and obtain a certificate of occupancy (certificat d'occupation) if required by municipal by-law. Software publishing under ISIC 6201 is not a classified industrial activity, so no industrial license is required; a virtual office with a registered agent is sufficient for a micro-SaaS.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or registered office service contract
Municipal zoning / occupancy certificate application
Fire safety attestation from the municipal fire department
Landlord consent for virtual office use, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses occupancy for zoning reasons, request a minor variance or relocate to premises that allow office use as of right; fire safety deficiencies are corrected and re-inspected at no extra administrative fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte aux changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) and CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the micro-SaaS does not require an environmental impact assessment or authorization under the Environment Quality Act. No discharge permit applies to cloud software services; office IT waste is subject to electronic waste recycling rules. If personnel are employed in Quebec, register as an employer with CNESST for workers' compensation coverage.
required_dossiers: Environmental exemption checklist for office activities
Employer registration with CNESST, if hiring staff
IT hardware disposal / recycling service agreement
Building compliance statement for server or equipment storage, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MELCCFP requires a declaration because the premises are classified, file an attestation of non-subjectivity and obtain a certificate of exemption. CNESST registration is mandatory before hiring; late registration may attract an administrative penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie du Québec (MEIE) — no industrial licence triggered for ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 software operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — software publishing and micro-SaaS operations are unlicensed business activities in Quebec

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte aux changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA, prior authorization, or certificate of authorization required for office-based cloud software services under section 22 of the Quebec Environment Quality Act unless the physical premises fall within a classified category
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOCs, or industrial air emissions are generated; the only applicable limits are municipal sanitary sewer and building ventilation standards for office tenancy; IT hardware disposal must comply with Quebec electronic waste recycling requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Commercial lease occupancy certificate issued by the local municipality; fire safety inspection and compliance certificate issued by the municipal fire service; structural loading declaration only if dedicated server/server-room equipment is installed; CNESST workplace health and safety registration for any Quebec personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal GST/HST, federal corporate income tax, and Business Number (BN) administration via My Business Account portal; Revenu Quebec - Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec corporate income tax, and enterprise registration through the Registraire des entreprises using the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act; no minimum capital is required and non-resident share ownership is permitted. 2) Obtain the Quebec NEQ automatically from the Registraire des entreprises upon provincial registration. 3) Register with CRA through Business Registration Online to obtain the 9-digit BN and open the GST/HST program account (BN-RR). 4) Register for QST with Revenu Quebec; for a Quebec-incorporated entity, the QST registration is coordinated with the provincial corporate file and the federal GST/HST registration. 5) Open payroll program accounts (CRA RP account and Revenu Quebec employer accounts) only if employees are present; a micro-SaaS operated through Paddle or Lemon Squeezy normally has no Canadian payroll. 6) Retain the BN and NEQ for payment-platform onboarding, banking, and export zero-rating documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; a Business Corporation is always a separate entity-level taxpayer under the Income Tax Act (ss. 89 and 248). Available elections include: (i) GST/HST group registration election under Excise Tax Act s. 273 and the parallel QST group election under the Quebec Sales Tax Act; (ii) Income Tax Act s. 93 election on the disposition of a foreign affiliate's taxable surplus; (iii) Income Tax Act s. 216 election for non-resident corporations earning specified Canadian rental income - not applicable to a resident Canadian operating company; and (iv) hybrid-mismatch deduction elections under recently enacted ITA ss. 18.2-18.4 implementing BEPS Action 2 for cross-border payments involving hybrid entities such as a US LLC. None of these mechanisms converts CA_CORP into a pass-through vehicle.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST/HST plus Quebec QST - a dual VAT-style consumption tax administered respectively by the Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148 and the Quebec Sales Tax Act: cumulative worldwide taxable supplies, including zero-rated exports, over four consecutive calendar quarters. Registration becomes mandatory once this threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration is available to a Quebec-incorporated corporation from day one. Under a genuine Merchant-of-Record contract, Paddle or Lemon Squeezy will collect and remit GST/HST and QST on Canadian consumer sales, but the developer's supply to the non-resident platform may still be counted for threshold purposes - the MoR agreement must clearly establish principal versus agent status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Canada and Quebec impose no national real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls, no digital stamping, and no mandatory API-based e-invoice validation. CRA and Revenu Quebec operate an audit-based documentary regime; PDF invoices and Paddle/Lemon Squeezy billing records are accepted. Voluntary e-invoicing follows the PEPPOL standard for federal procurement, and Quebec's certified sales recording module (SRM) applies only to designated point-of-sale sectors, not to ISIC 6201 SaaS operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to SaaS supplied to a non-resident for use entirely outside Canada under ETA Schedule VI Part IV s. 6 (exported intangible personal property) and Part V s. 7 (services to non-residents), mirrored by Quebec QST zero-rating rules. Core criteria: the recipient is a non-resident with no Canadian establishment; the SaaS is not used in connection with real or tangible property located in Canada; billing address, payment instrument, and IP geolocation all point outside Canada; and, in Merchant-of-Record sales, Paddle or Lemon Squeezy acquires title and resells to end customers. Zero-rated export revenue counts as a taxable supply for the CAD 30,000 registration threshold.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Goods-only export evidence (not applicable to pure digital SaaS): CBSA Customs Export Declaration (CADEX/ACI eManifest) and Bill of Lading/Air Waybill; no customs filing is required for SaaS delivered electronically.

Digital substantiation bundle: executed SaaS subscription or master licence agreement with the non-resident customer or Merchant of Record; invoices issued to the non-resident party; customer attestation of non-Canadian residence and place of use.

Payment and FX evidence: Paddle/Lemon Squeezy payout and settlement statements, inward remittance records, foreign-currency bank receipts, and FX conversion confirmations; plus IP-geolocation and access logs demonstrating non-Canadian download and use.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA Export Review and Revenu Quebec audits closely scrutinize zero-rating claims. If denied, the supplier is reassessed for uncollected GST (5%) plus QST (9.975% on the GST-inclusive base) with retroactive effect within the four-year reassessment period (ETA s. 298 and Quebec Tax Administration Act), which is extended indefinitely for misrepresentation or fraud. Civil penalties include a 50% gross-negligence penalty on the tax or refund amount under ETA s. 285.1 and the corresponding Quebec provision. Criminal tax evasion under ETA s. 327 and the Quebec Tax Administration Act carries fines up to CAD 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years on indictment. Input tax credits and QST input tax refunds attributable to the claimed export sale are clawed back; if the Merchant-of-Record relationship is recharacterized as agency, CRA and Revenu Quebec may additionally assess unremitted GST/HST/QST on all Canadian consumer SaaS sales processed by Paddle or Lemon Squeezy, with compounded daily arrears interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange-control authority imposing currency conversion, capital-repatriation, or export-proceeds-surrender controls. Anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing compliance is administered principally by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), while cross-border currency reporting is administered by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary commercial, investment, and treasury transactions. Canada generally has no capital-account approval requirement, exchange-control registration, mandatory use of domestic currency, or general restriction on repatriation of dividends, interest, royalties, loan principal, or liquidation proceeds. Current-account payments are not subject to routine foreign-exchange licensing. Remittances remain subject to corporate-law authorization, solvency requirements, applicable withholding tax, transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds checks, sanctions screening, lender or escrow restrictions, and bank documentation requirements. Payments involving restricted jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, unusual payment chains, or high-risk virtual-asset activity may be delayed or rejected. Quebec corporations must also consider applicable Quebec corporate-law approvals and French-language documentation requirements where relevant to local operations and contracting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a domestic bank, convert export receipts into Canadian dollars, or convert a prescribed percentage within a fixed period. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the corporation's discretion. Exporters must comply with applicable customs, export-control, sanctions, GST/HST, income-tax, accounting, and contractual requirements. Financial institutions must report certain international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, or equivalent, to FINTRAC when the applicable reporting conditions are met; this is a reporting obligation and not a conversion or repatriation requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for merchant collection and payout functions, subject to provider eligibility and underwriting; Low as a complete substitute for a Canadian domestic operating bank. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy generally operate as merchant-of-record or payment-platform providers rather than ordinary Canadian deposit-taking banks. They may collect subscription revenue, calculate or facilitate indirect taxes, and remit net proceeds to the corporation, but account availability, supported countries, currencies, payout destinations, reserves, chargeback treatment, prohibited-business rules, and customer-verification standards are contractual. They do not normally provide unrestricted deposit-taking, Canadian cheque services, domestic payroll functionality, or a guaranteed corporate banking relationship. The corporation must accurately identify the merchant of record, beneficial owner, operating location, software product, customer geography, refund policy, data practices, and tax registrations. Use of an offshore EMI or payment account does not eliminate Canadian corporate income-tax, GST/HST, Quebec sales-tax, transfer-pricing, sanctions, or AML obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks may permit remote onboarding for a corporation, particularly where the corporation, directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners have readily verifiable Canadian identities and addresses. Physical attendance is not universally mandated by statute, but a bank may require an in-person meeting, video interview, notarized or certified documents, Canadian address evidence, or a branch visit based on risk, non-resident ownership, unusual ownership chains, foreign funding, remote-only operations, or inability to verify identity electronically. Directors do not automatically need to appear physically merely because the corporation is Quebec-based. The bank determines the final onboarding method under applicable customer-identification, beneficial-ownership, sanctions, and AML procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, layered foreign holding companies, or inconsistent corporate registers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles and certificate of incorporation, current corporate profile or Quebec enterprise register extract, bylaws, directors and officers register, complete ownership chart to each natural-person beneficial owner, shareholder register, ownership percentages, passports or government identification, residential-address evidence, and a signed beneficial-ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder funding described only as a generic transfer or unexplained capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and shareholder resolutions, executed subscription agreement or shareholder-loan agreement, capitalization table, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, remitter-bank confirmation, transfer-pricing analysis where applicable, wire instructions identifying the legal purpose, and accounting treatment showing equity or debt classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote-only Micro-SaaS business with no demonstrated customers, revenue, personnel, or operating substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Website and product demonstration, software ownership or licensing evidence, subscription terms, privacy policy, customer invoices, payment-processor statements, contracts, projected transaction volumes, business plan, vendor agreements, incorporation records, tax registrations where applicable, and explanation of expected geographies and currencies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or opaque payment flows through Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, other payment intermediaries, virtual-asset platforms, or unrelated third-party accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant-of-record agreement, processor statements, payout reports, settlement-account ownership evidence, customer and refund-flow description, chargeback controls, sanctions-screening procedures, reconciliation schedule, and written confirmation that funds are not held for or transmitted on behalf of unrelated third parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction activity inconsistent with a lightweight productivity SaaS profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast, monthly transaction-volume and value estimates by corridor, customer concentration analysis, recurring-revenue schedule, explanation of refunds and chargebacks, payroll and vendor budget, tax remittance calendar, and documented approval thresholds for unusual payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign directors or owners lacking Canadian residential or operating ties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid identification, residential and business-address verification, immigration or corporate-residency information where relevant, management-service agreements, local registered-office evidence, Canadian tax and corporate filings, explanation of decision-making location, and video or in-person verification if requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, or high-risk-jurisdiction match
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full identity-resolution package, legal-name and alias analysis, source-of-wealth evidence, independent corporate records, transaction rationale, sanctions-screening results, written legal assessment where a false positive is identified, and enhanced monitoring commitments. A genuine sanctions match cannot be cured by documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to evidence control over the software, customer data, or intellectual property
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Software-development agreements, assignment instruments, repository or deployment evidence, trademark or domain ownership, employee and contractor IP assignments, cloud-service contracts, customer terms, and data-processing documentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route funds directly from the identified shareholder, parent, or lender bank account to the Canadian corporation's account at the receiving institution. Use a payment narrative such as 'equity subscription,' 'shareholder loan,' or 'intercompany loan' only when supported by executed documents. Canada does not use a universal central-bank purpose-code regime for ordinary corporate capital inflows; the bank may nevertheless require an internal purpose classification and supporting documents. Provide the corporation's exact legal name, account number, institution and transit details, SWIFT/BIC where applicable, remitter identity, ultimate beneficial owner, agreement date, currency, amount, and expected use of proceeds. Avoid third-party funding and split transfers designed to evade monitoring. Reconcile the incoming wire to the general ledger, issue shares or record debt consistently with the documents, assess thin-capitalization and transfer-pricing implications, and preserve records for tax, audit, and AML purposes. International electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, or equivalent, may trigger financial-institution reporting to FINTRAC; the corporation should not attempt to structure transfers to avoid reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary SaaS expenses, use bank wires, international electronic funds transfers, EFT, bill-payment rails, or corporate cards to verified suppliers. A SWIFT MT103 customer-credit-transfer message may be used for an international wire where supported by the sending and receiving banks; obtain the payment confirmation, value date, beneficiary details, intermediary-bank information, and fee allocation. For substantial or documentary trade purchases, a commercial letter of credit may be issued or advised through a Canadian bank, with documentary conditions matching the underlying contract. A letter of credit is generally unnecessary for routine software subscriptions, cloud hosting, contractors, and digital advertising. Screen beneficiaries, banks, jurisdictions, and goods or services against applicable Canadian sanctions and export-control requirements; retain invoices, contracts, purchase approvals, proof of delivery or service, tax treatment, and foreign-exchange records. Apply withholding-tax analysis to cross-border interest, royalties, software rights, management fees, and certain services before payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD or CAD/other-currency forward contracts with a regulated Canadian bank or other appropriately authorized counterparty, supported by a documented underlying exposure, treasury policy, counterparty limit, confirmation, maturity, settlement instructions, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards may be used for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to counterparty eligibility, derivatives documentation, applicable Canadian securities and derivatives rules, collateral terms, suitability and disclosure requirements, and the legality of the reference currency and settlement structure. NDFs are not normally required for freely convertible CAD exposure.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps may be used for recurring or longer-term funding exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, credit support, valuation, collateral, termination, accounting, tax, and board-approval controls.

Foreign-currency accounts and natural hedges may be used to match foreign-currency subscription receipts with hosting, contractor, advertising, and other operating costs; this is liquidity management rather than a derivative and remains subject to bank terms and internal controls.

Currency options or collars may be considered for asymmetric exposures, subject to documented risk limits, premium approval, counterparty authorization, fair-value and accounting controls, and a strict prohibition on speculative transactions unrelated to identifiable business exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises (REQ), Government of Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the enterprise registration in the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and interest per REQ tariff; administrative strike-off from the Quebec enterprise register after one year of sustained non-compliance, resulting in loss of juridical personality until revived

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if federally incorporated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may lead to a notice from Corporations Canada and administrative dissolution after one year of continued delinquency; reinstatement fees and revival conditions apply

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory revenue- or asset-based threshold for a non-distributing private corporation; a statutory audit is required for a reporting issuer or public company, and must otherwise be appointed unless all shareholders consent in writing to dispense with an auditor for the financial year. Certain minority shareholders exercising statutory rights may require an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; private enterprises may elect IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). The annual financial statements presenting under the relevant statute must be prepared in accordance with the chosen framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For federally incorporated corporations, maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control and confirm the register when filing the Corporations Canada annual return; record any change in significant control within 15 days of the change. For Quebec-registered enterprises, disclose ultimate beneficial owner information in the annual declaration and notify REQ within 30 days of any ultimate beneficiary change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100-450 typical annual fee for a registered agent or virtual corporate office in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500-8,000 if a full independent audit is required; USD 1,000-3,000 for a review engagement if the audit is dispensed with

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporation tax rate (Canada federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); 12.2% combined rate applies to qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) active business income up to CA$500,000 per year
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad statutory tax holiday applies. Preferential mechanics: CCPC small business deduction reduces the combined active business rate to 12.2% on the first CA$500,000; federal SR&ED refundable investment tax credit at 35% of eligible Canadian research and development expenditures for CCPCs; Quebec refundable R&D tax credit; Quebec Innovation tax incentives; patent income deduction available for qualifying IP exploitation; eligible cloud software development costs may be claimed as Canadian SR&ED expenditures if technical uncertainty and systematic investigation are evident.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — Federal, filed via CRA approved EFILE software, CRA Corporation Internet Filing, or by a registered tax preparer; Revenu Québec receives provincial data through the federal-provincial tax collection agreement except where the Quebec CO-17 is separately due.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; each corporation must file a T2 return for every taxation year, even if no tax is payable and even if it is inactive. Instalment payments are generally required quarterly or monthly if the prior-year federal/Quebec tax balance exceeds prescribed thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed no later than six months after the end of the corporation's taxation year. Quebec CO-17 filing deadline is also the last day of the sixth month following fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, Business Number (BN), taxation year-end, jurisdiction of incorporation, registered office address, postal code, principal business activity and NAICS code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment, state the Canadian permanent establishment address and the Canadian agent or statutory representative. If the central mind and management is outside Canada, disclose director residencies and the place of board decisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, revenues and subscription income, including MRR/ARR from cloud SaaS, licence revenue, and any ancillary services, reconciled to payment processor settlement statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income attributable to the Canadian business if the corporation is a non-resident relying on a treaty permanent establishment; otherwise worldwide income is reported for a resident corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and direct hosting costs: cloud infrastructure, third-party database services, support costs, payment processor fees, and development resources capitalized where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only costs incurred to earn the reported Canadian-source income. Cross-border cost allocations must be supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation and Form T106 where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income for tax purposes before loss carryovers, after operating expenses, depreciation/capital cost allowance, amortization of intangible assets, and any applicable reserve adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations should attach a reconciliation of book income to Canadian taxable income and identify any deemed Canadian-source income under Income Tax Act provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation, federal small business deduction, general rate reduction, foreign tax credits, investment tax credits, and the calculation of federal Part I tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation does not claim the CCPC small business deduction; it should compute federal tax on Canadian-source active business income through a permanent establishment and claim only treaty-appropriate deductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% for each full month late, up to 12 months. For a second or subsequent failure within three years, the penalty increases to 10% plus 2% per month, capped at 24 months. CRA also charges daily compound interest at prescribed rates. Repeated failure permits arbitrary assessment and loss of deduction or credit rights.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return — Quebec, filed with Revenu Québec via the EDEN electronic filing system or approved tax preparation software; Quebec corporations with a permanent establishment in Quebec must file CO-17 even when the T2 is filed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; instalments for Quebec income tax are due quarterly or monthly when prior-year provincial tax payable exceeds Revenu Québec thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17 must be filed no later than the last day of the sixth month after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation name, Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), business number, fiscal year-end, legal jurisdiction of incorporation, permanent establishment address, principal industrial activity code (ISIC/NAICS).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a permanent establishment in Quebec must identify the Quebec permanent establishment and any representative having authority to receive notices, and file all required schedules for Canadian-source income allocated to Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income under the Quebec Taxation Act, including reconciliation from the federal T2 taxable income to Quebec taxable income: differences in depreciation, deductions, SR&ED credits, and loss carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Quebec allocation formula for income attributable to the Quebec permanent establishment; include only expenses deductible under the Taxation Act and provide transfer-pricing documentation for inter-provincial or cross-border charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 — Deductions and Tax Credits Section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec small business deduction for CCPC active business income, Quebec SR&ED deduction and refundable R&D tax credits, innovation tax credits, other refundable credits, and any provincial tax holiday or eligibility disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled corporations generally cannot claim Quebec small business deductions unless they remain Canadian-controlled private corporations; a foreign parent's status and actual board control must be disclosed accurately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Quebec income tax, instalment credits, refundable credits, balance due or refund, and any prescribed penalties or interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the corporation is exempt from Quebec income tax under a treaty or statutory provision, attach the exemption authority; otherwise remit any balance due by the deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec assesses a late filing penalty of 5% of the balance unpaid plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months; repeated or grossly negligent failure attracts higher penalties and daily compound interest. Revenu Québec may also reassess arbitrarily and impose statutory liens on Quebec property and bank accounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident of Canada, before application of any tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: DTA relief is not automatic. The non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Canadian payer with a completed CRA Form NR301 (Declaration of Exemption from Withholding) or equivalent, together with a valid foreign Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) confirming residence in the treaty jurisdiction. The payer must withhold and remit the treaty-reduced rate only if the documentation is in order before payment; if the full 25% was withheld because documentation arrived late, the non-resident may file CRA Form NR7-R for a refund. Retain all TRCs and NR301 declarations for six years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for interest, royalty, and similar amounts paid or credited to a non-resident. Treaty rates vary: the Canada-United States treaty commonly reduces royalties and interest to 0-15%, depending on the nature of the royalty (copyright vs. trademark), the beneficial ownership, whether the recipient is a related party, and whether the interest is arm's length contingent interest. For all treaty reductions, the recipient must have economic substance and provide a TRC plus the appropriate withholding declaration before the distribution is remitted.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CA$1,000,000 of aggregate consideration for non-arm's length transactions with non-residents triggers the formal contemporaneous documentation requirement and the CRA Form T106 reporting obligation; a master/local file package is expected under CRA Transfer Pricing Memorandum when controlled transaction exposure exceeds CA$1,000,000, and Country-by-Country Report thresholds apply to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of CA$750,000,000 or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations to ordinary operating corporations. However, CRA and Revenu Québec apply the substance-over-form doctrine, the business-purpose test, and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Income Tax Act section 245 to deny tax benefits from transactions lacking commercial or economic substance. A Canadian micro-SaaS corporation must maintain genuine operational oversight in Canada: real board decisions, substantively located personnel, Canadian bank accounts, written contracts, and auditable books; otherwise it may be recharacterized as a conduit or deemed to have a permanent establishment or foreign residence for its beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly or through gross negligence making false or deceptive statements in the T2 or CO-17 return, underreporting SaaS subscription revenue, fabricating expenses, concealing payment processor settlements, destroying books, or evading the assessment or payment of tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under Income Tax Act section 239(1): fine of at least 50% and up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, plus imprisonment for up to two years on summary conviction. Civil gross-negligence penalty under Income Tax Act section 163(2) equals 50% of the understated tax. Revenu Québec imposes equivalent penalties under the Taxation Act, together with daily compound interest and the loss of all loss carryovers or credit claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct, authorize, assent to, or acquiesce in false filings are personally liable as parties to the offence and may be convicted and imprisoned. Under the CBCA and QBCA, directors have an overarching fiduciary duty to ensure the corporation maintains accurate records; deliberate falsification permits piercing the corporate veil and personal civil restitution to the Crown. A director defending an evasion prosecution cannot shelter behind the corporate entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unremitted Source Deductions, QST and Payroll Liabilities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Collecting employee income tax, Canada Pension Plan contributions, Employment Insurance premiums, GST/HST, or Quebec QST and failing to remit those trust amounts on their statutory due dates; using payroll or QST trust funds for operating expenses or owner distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Directors' liability assessment under Income Tax Act section 227.1 and Excise Tax Act section 323, with parallel liability under Quebec Taxation Act and QST Act for the full unremitted amount, plus interest and penalties. CRA and Revenu Québec may garnish personal bank accounts, impose liens on personal property, and deny discharge from tax debts in insolvency where trust amounts were misappropriated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Statutory director liability is automatic where the corporation fails to remit; no fraud is required. Each director and former director can be assessed personally and jointly and severally. Directors may be barred from leaving Canada on outstanding trust-fund assessments and may face criminal prosecution for intentional failure to remit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing, Profit Stripping and Management Fee Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's length royalties, SaaS licence fees, service fees, or interest to a foreign related corporation in a zero-tax jurisdiction without contemporaneous documentation; routing subscription revenue through an IP-holding entity with no employees, substance, or commercial activity; backdated cost-sharing arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA and Revenu Québec may recharacterize consideration to the arm's length amount under Income Tax Act section 247(2); a transfer-pricing penalty equal to 10% of the net upward adjustment applies where the adjustment exceeds the prescribed threshold and no adequate contemporaneous documentation exists. Part XIII withholding can also be assessed at 25% on deemed dividends, royalties, interest, or management fees paid to non-residents, with interest compounded daily.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false transfer-pricing documentation or orchestrate sham intercompany transactions may be prosecuted for tax evasion. The courts may disregard the corporate veil where a wholly-owned IP-holding vehicle is a mere façade, leaving the director and controlling shareholder personally liable for the tax adjustment and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Sham Substance and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Canadian corporation as a facade with no real office, no bank account, no employees, no commercial activity, or where all board decisions and core business functions occur outside Canada; incorporating solely to access treaty benefits, favourable tax rates, or to avoid a permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Income Tax Act section 245 disallows the tax benefit; Revenu Québec applies a parallel GAAR. Treaty benefits may be denied under the applicable DTA's limitation-on-benefits or beneficial ownership clause, and the corporation can be reassessed as a non-resident or as a permanent establishment of a foreign principal. Penalties include 50% of the amount of the misreporting plus interest; criminal tax evasion applies if deceit is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who allow a shell corporation to be used for tax avoidance are exposed to personal assessments for unremitted withholding or payroll trust amounts, and where the corporation is a sham, creditors and the tax authorities can pierce the veil. Directors can face prohibition from managing corporations, asset freezing, civil restitution, and imprisonment for knowingly participating in a sham or fraudulent arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Payment Processor Misuse and Off-Book Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Paddle or Lemon Squeezy subscription payments while deliberately omitting chargeback refunds, intermingling founder personal accounts with corporate SaaS revenue, creating false merchant identities, structuring merchant settlements to avoid reporting thresholds, or laundering proceeds through cryptocurrency or shell accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Criminal Code of Canada, laundering proceeds of crime is an indictable offence carrying up to ten years' imprisonment. Income Tax Act section 239 penalties apply to false books and omission of revenue: 50% to 200% of the tax evaded plus imprisonment. The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act authorizes large administrative monetary penalties and criminal sanctions for evasion of reporting requirements. Civil reassessment, gross negligence penalties, and compound interest apply regardless of criminal outcome.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors participate criminally if they knowingly direct or tolerate payment-processing misconduct; personal convictions carry imprisonment. Separate from criminal liability, AML/OFAC sanctions violations and statutory director liability for unpaid corporate tax can be assessed directly against directors. Where the corporate shell is merely a conduit for diverted funds, courts will order disgorgement and civil restitution against the controlling director and permit attachment of personal assets.
